title: Peek startup takes a long time

judgment.rationale: The discussion and logs point to an elevated Runner starting non-elevated Peek while many modules initialize concurrently. That is a plausible, reproducible startup interaction, but the evidence does not yet prove whether the delay is expected process/UAC overhead or an avoidable serialization/regression.
judgment.recommended_action: Measure the startup timeline with elevated and non-elevated Runner modes, then decide whether a code change is warranted rather than optimizing from a single trace.

evidence.fact: The issue reports high Peek startup latency and includes logs showing "Starting Peek non elevated from elevated process" amid a long module startup sequence.
The discussion recommends not running PowerToys elevated or starting it earlier, indicating an elevation/UAC interaction may be central.
Runner starts enabled modules during startup, so Peek launch timing is coupled to global module initialization.

fix_assessment.rationale: The likely interaction is identifiable, but measured baseline and desired startup threshold are missing, so optimization confidence is moderate.

proposed_fixes.title: Reduce avoidable Peek startup blocking after Runner elevation handoff
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The startup sequence may make Peek readiness wait behind elevated Runner/module initialization and a non-elevated child-process launch, but the dominant cost is not yet measured.
plan: Instrument Runner and Peek launch/readiness timestamps without collecting private user content.
Compare serial and independent module startup costs in elevated and non-elevated modes.
Change orchestration only where the measured critical path is avoidable, preserving process ownership and security boundaries.
verification: The original slow cold-start scenario is measured and improves to the agreed threshold.
All enabled modules still start and the elevation boundary remains intact.

confidence.rationale: The log identifies a credible startup interaction, but no timing baseline or target threshold is provided.

issue_context.summary: Peek can take a long time to become usable when PowerToys runs elevated and launches Peek non-elevated while other modules start.
known_information: The report includes a startup log sequence and maintainer guidance about elevation/start timing.
Runner starts enabled modules during startup.
No confirmed public fix or measured threshold was identified.
inferences: The delay may be dominated by process creation/UAC and concurrent module initialization rather than Peek preview code.
A code change should be justified by a controlled timing comparison.
issue_context.analysis: Capture cold and warm startup timings in supported elevation modes and isolate the Peek process creation interval.

information_gaps.information: Cold-start timing for elevated versus non-elevated Runner, including the interval from Runner launch to Peek readiness and whether the delay repeats after warm start.
information_gaps.why_needed: Without a baseline and threshold, it is not possible to distinguish expected elevation overhead from a regression worth changing.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once in each supported elevation mode and run /bugreport after Peek becomes ready, noting cold versus warm start.

actions.label: Request targeted evidence
actions.note: Establish a measurable baseline before changing startup orchestration.

comment.body: The supplied log confirms that Runner starts Peek non-elevated from an elevated process during a long multi-module startup, but it does not establish how much of the delay is expected UAC/process creation overhead. Please capture cold-start timings for elevated and non-elevated Runner modes, record the time from Runner launch to Peek readiness, and say whether a warm restart is also slow. Run /bugreport after a reproduced slow start so the timing can be correlated with the module sequence.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Measure and, only if warranted, decouple Peek readiness from unrelated module startup or reduce avoidable elevation handoff overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start Peek readiness meets an agreed threshold in supported elevation modes.
Unrelated module initialization does not block Peek unnecessarily.
Non-elevated and elevated behavior preserve existing security and ownership semantics.
